review_candidates.description: Company Description Eatery is a dynamic food hub that combines a restaurant, cooking school, incubator, and community space in one location. It serves as a food and cooking theater where guests engage with local and international chefs, food suppliers, and food critics. The venue hosts food cultural events that showcase emerging concepts and ideas from across the culinary industry. Eatery fosters collaboration, creativity, and learning for food enthusiasts and professionals. Team members join a vibrant environment focused on shared experiences and innovation in food culture. Role Description The Cost Control Specialist is a full-time, on-site role based in Giza, responsible for monitoring and optimizing food and operational costs across Eatery’s restaurant and cooking school activities. This role involves tracking daily expenditures, analyzing cost data, and preparing regular cost reports for management. The specialist will collaborate with kitchen, purchasing, and operations teams to review consumption patterns, negotiate with suppliers as needed, and ensure adherence to cost control policies. They will support budgeting and forecasting processes, identify cost-saving opportunities, and contribute to pricing decisions for menu items and culinary events. The position also includes maintaining accurate cost records, ensuring compliance with financial standards, and recommending process improvements to enhance profitability without compromising quality or guest experience. Qualifications Strong cost control and cost management skills, with experience in monitoring and optimizing operational and food-related expenses. Proficiency in cost reporting and cost accounting, including preparing detailed cost analyses, dashboards, and management reports. Advanced analytical skills with the ability to interpret financial data, identify trends, and propose practical cost-saving measures. Experience in hospitality, restaurant operations, or food service environments is highly beneficial. Ability to work on-site in Giza, collaborate with cross-functional teams, and communicate clearly with culinary and management staff. Competence in Excel or other financial analysis tools; familiarity with ERP or restaurant management systems is a plus. Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Attention to detail, integrity in handling financial information, and a proactive approach to problem-solving and process improvement.

Design and implement surveys, evaluations, sampling methodologies, indicators, and digital data collection tools using platforms such as KoboToolbox, SurveyCTO, or ODK. Develop and apply appropriate monitoring, evaluation, data collection, and verification methodologies, including on-site, virtual, and secondary data collection approaches. Oversee field data collection and quality control team to ensure quality processes are implemented, providing technical guidance on data validation, integrity, and analytical standards. Analyze program data to identify trends, patterns, compliance issues, lessons learned, and opportunities for improvement, and translate findings into actionable recommendations, analytical reports, dashboards, data visualizations, and other reporting products for donors, funders, and management. Provide DME support to equipment- and asset-focused programs, including assessing the utilization, accountability, and impact of U.S. Government-provided equipment and other program assets, where applicable. Provide technical guidance to program staff and ensure activities and data management comply with applicable quality control mechanisms as well as donor, contractual, information security, and data protection requirements. Perform other duties as assigned. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s degree in evaluation, statistics, social science, international development, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience. Minimum of five years of professional experience in design, monitoring and evaluation, including at least two years designing and implementing M&E programs. Fluency in Ukrainian written and verbal and English. Demonstrated professional experience in design, monitoring and evaluation, including statistically valid sampling methodology, survey instrument design, and digital data collection using platforms such as KoboToolbox, SurveyCTO, or ODK. Demonstrated experience producing analytical reports and data visualizations for donor or funder audiences. Technical proficiency in conducting monitoring and evaluation activities. Ability to obtain INL Kyiv approval as Key Personnel prior to job offer. Ability to satisfy background check requirements. Physical and medical fitness for field travel under operational conditions in Ukraine. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Master's degree in evaluation, statistics, social science, international development, or a related field. Seven or more years of design, monitoring and evaluation experience on donor-funded programs. Prior experience with U.S. Government funded programs and familiarity with end-use monitoring or property accountability frameworks. Experience conducting evaluation work in conflict-affected or post-conflict operating environments. Proficiency in statistical analysis software and in Power BI or comparable visualization tooling. Familiarity with the Ministry of the Interior, including the National Police of Ukraine, the State Border Guard Service, or the National Guard of Ukraine.
